device.body: A computer, server or phone that has been registered on the network.

network.body: The set of registered devices that can communicate with each other under the rules.

registration.body: The step that authorises a device to join the network.

overlayAddress.body: The private address a device uses inside the network: it does not work on the public internet.

publicKey.body: A code that identifies a device and lets others check it really is that device.

posture.body: Checks on the device's state, such as encrypted disk, firewall and system version.

notReported.body: The device has not sent this information yet: it does not mean it failed the check.

attestation.body: Proof signed by the device itself that confirms its security features.

quarantine.body: The device stays registered but cannot communicate with the others until the block is removed.

revoke.body: The device is disconnected and its key is no longer accepted: this cannot be undone.

subnetwork.body: A separate group of devices: those in the same sub-network can see each other; others cannot until they are connected.

accessRules.body: The list that decides which devices may communicate, by address and port. If no rule allows it, communication is blocked.

blockingRule.body: A rule that discards traffic between two given addresses without notifying anyone.

rules.body: The settings that decide which links are allowed. They do not prove that data is flowing.

path.body: The route data follows from one device to another, through the network or a relay.

measuredPath.body: A link confirmed by real measurements between two devices.

networkLink.body: An agreement between two independent networks that lets some of their devices communicate.

signedCode.body: A code with a digital signature: the recipient can check it came from the other side and was not changed.

peer.body: Another device this one can communicate with.

traffic.body: How much data passes through the network at a given moment.

responseTime.body: The time a message takes to travel to a device and back, in milliseconds.

responseVariation.body: How much response time changes from one message to the next: less variation means a steadier link.

relay.body: A device that forwards other devices' traffic when they cannot reach each other directly.

derp.body: A server that forwards encrypted data between two devices that cannot connect directly, for example behind strict firewalls.

internetExit.body: A device that sends network traffic out to the public internet.

userDevice.body: A device a person uses to connect, which does not forward traffic for others.

onion.body: Traffic passes through three stops, each with its own encryption layer: no single stop knows both the sender and the destination. In NeroNet this is not active yet.

keyExchange.body: The first exchange of messages in which two devices identify themselves and agree on a shared key.

contactAddress.body: The address another network uses to reach ours.

addressRange.body: A way to write a group of addresses: for example 100.64.0.0/16 covers all addresses from 100.64.0.0 to 100.64.255.255.

hiddenGroup.body: A group of devices that stays invisible until the unlock password is entered.

group.body: Devices collected together, so they can be shown or hidden as a single entry.

responseWindow.body: The time a device has to answer in order to count as reachable.

controlServer.body: The server that runs the network: it registers devices and distributes the rules.

riskScore.body: A number estimating how risky a device's behaviour looks. Above 75 it is flagged as high risk.

padding.body: Filler data that makes every message the same length, so its content is not revealed. In NeroNet this is not active yet.

connectionTest.body: A test message that measures how long a device takes to answer.

withoutAdminRights.body: The device runs the software without the system's highest permissions, which limits damage if it is breached.

noiseScheme.body: The specific key exchange scheme used by encrypted links between devices.

xchacha.body: The mathematical method that protects data from being read by third parties.

acl.body: A list of rules that decides which devices may talk to each other and on which ports. Nothing is allowed unless a rule allows it.

defaultDeny.body: If no rule covers traffic, that traffic is blocked.

defaultOpen.body: If no rule covers traffic, that traffic is allowed.

zeroTrust.body: A model in which no device is trusted just because it is already on the network: every connection must be checked.

packetTest.body: A test that says whether a single data packet would pass, without actually sending it.

compiledPolicy.body: The rules already translated into the format each device applies.

policyVersion.body: A number that goes up with each rule change. It shows which version each device has.

auditChain.body: Each log entry contains the fingerprint of the one before, so a change shows up.

hmac.body: A cryptographic fingerprint that proves data was not altered without the secret key.

checkpoint.body: A signed photograph of the log's state, to compare with later.

ed25519.body: The type of signature the system uses for snapshots and the transparency signal.

siem.body: An external security monitoring system that receives and analyses events.

mfa.body: A second check at sign-in: a 6-digit code that changes every 30 seconds and comes from the app on your phone.

recoveryCode.body: An emergency code to sign in if you lose your phone. It works only once.

rbac.body: Role-based access control: each role grants a specific set of permissions.

cryptoShredding.body: The keys that protect the data are erased for good: without keys, the data cannot be read.

dualAuthorization.body: A sensitive action needs the approval of two different people.

legalHold.body: A legal obligation that prevents an organisation's data from being erased until it is removed.

deadMansSwitch.body: A check that carries out an action (here: erasure) if the owner does not confirm they are present within a set time.

warrantCanary.body: A signed signal updated regularly: if it stops being updated, something may have happened.

splitTunneling.body: Some apps are excluded from the protected tunnel and connect directly to the internet.

netmap.body: The list of devices and rules a device keeps. The limit says how long it uses it without contacting the network.

heartbeat.body: The regular check-in in which each device confirms to the network that it is active.

tenant.body: An isolated organisation within the network, with its own devices and users.

sso.body: Single sign-on: the user signs in with their work account, without a separate console password.

pkce.body: A protection for single sign-on that stops the access code from being stolen.

dns.body: DNS links a site name to its address; CNAME is an alias between two names; TLS is site encryption (the padlock); FQDN is a domain's full name.

webrtc.body: The technology that streams video and inputs directly between two devices in a browser.

ice.body: Procedures by which two devices find the most direct path to talk, even behind a router.

vcpu.body: Virtual processors, a type of fast disk, a virtual computer's graphics card.

codec.body: The format in which video is compressed for transmission.

preAuthKey.body: A one-time key that authorises a device to join the network.

wireguardConfig.body: The file (or QR code) that connects a device to the WireGuard tunnel.

wireguard.body: The encrypted tunnel protocol used to connect devices.

node.body: A device registered on the network. In the text, use 'device'.

mebibyte.body: A unit of data equal to 1,048,576 bytes, slightly more than a megabyte.

super-admin.body: Manages every organisation on this server.

owner.body: Has full control of the organisation, including erasing its data.

admin.body: Manages users, devices and rules in the organisation.

network_admin.body: Manages devices, access rules and registration keys, but not users.

auditor.body: Reads devices, rules and the activity log, and cannot change anything.

member.body: Uses the network and sees their own devices.

user.body: Uses the network and sees their own devices.
